To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diagonalization of BS structures in CAM variable λt is possible, that the existence of leading Reggéons terms is strictly conditioned by a global Bethe Salpeter kernel and the existence of BS equations is strictly conditioned by analyticity properties of the four point function in the crossed channels.

(i) the CAM representation of the BS structure is diagonalized in λt, (ii) the diagonalized BS structure is a convolution equation with a spectral kernel, and (iii) the leading Reggeon term in the asymptotic expansion is a solution of a convolution equation with the same spectral kernel.

(a) the general t-channel BS structure of a fourpoint function can be diagonalized for all negative values t, and (b) this diagonalization is closely connected with the existence of BSequations for the absorptivity in the crossed channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the general properties of the BS-equations in the CAM representation, and their relation with the existence of Regge poles and their asymptotic properties, in the framework of local relativistic QFT.
the analytic properties of the BS-structure of the four-point functions, which can be expressed in terms of the CAM variable λt.
the general properties of four-point functions, and in particular of their absorptive parts, in the framework of QFT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAM representation of four-point functions is the most appropriate one for the analysis of their asymptotic behaviour in the crossed channels.
the Regge pole structure of QFT is an unavoidable consequence of the axiomatic framework and of the analyticity properties of QFT.
the CAM diagonalization is an analytic property of the BS structure of the four-point functions in a general local relativistic QFT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CAM representation of four-point functions is the natural framework to study the analyticity and the asymptotic properties of QFT.
the CAM-diagonalization of the BS-structure of the four-point functions is an analytic tool to investigate the asymptotic behaviour at fixed t of a general QFT.
the CAM representation of four-point functions is the natural arena for the description of Reggeon terms, and for the analysis of the Regge limit of QFT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analytic properties of the BS structure are intimately related to the existence in the crossed channels of convolution equations, which are the basis for the derivation of the BS-equations.

the diagonalization of BS-structures in CAM variables is a powerful tool for the study of the analytic structure of QFT, in particular for the identification and classification of Reggeons and their couplings.
the diagonalization of this kernel in the λt variable is the key step in the proof of Regge behaviour.
